notes.summary: Statistics in Quant covers mean, median, mode and range for small data sets. 0–1 questions in Tier 1, 1–2 in Tier 2.

concepts.title: Mean
concepts.body: Mean = sum of observations / number of observations. For a frequency table, mean = Σfx / Σf.

concepts.title: Median and mode
concepts.body: Median: arrange in order; middle value (odd n) or average of the two middle values (even n). Mode: the value that occurs most often.

concepts.title: Empirical relation
concepts.body: For a moderately skewed distribution: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean.

varieties.name: Mean and corrected mean
varieties.how: Work with the total; fix wrong entries by subtracting the wrong value and adding the right one.

varieties.name: Median and mode
varieties.how: Sort the data first; count frequencies for mode.

tips: Always sort before finding the median.
For a frequency table, multiply each value by its frequency before adding.
traps: For an even count, the median is the average of the two middle values.
Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean, not 3 Mean − 2 Median.

questions.q: What is the mean of 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20?
Find the mode of the data: 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 7, 7, 8, 9.
questions.solution:
3 occurs twice, 7 occurs three times, the rest once.
Mode = 7.

questions.q: The mean of 10 observations is 20. Later it was found that one observation, 25, was wrongly copied as 52. What is the correct mean?
For a moderately skewed distribution, the mean is 30 and the median is 28. What is the mode (approximately)?
Find the mean of the following data — values (x): 10, 20, 30, 40; frequencies (f): 3, 5, 8, 4.

flashcards.back: Average of the two middle values
